'''Jerome Jordan''' (born September 29, 1986), is an [[Jamaican]] [[college basketball]] center for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]].

Jordan selected Tulsa over [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]] and [[Stetson University]], enrolling in the 2006-07 school year.<ref name="ap">[[Associated Press]]. [http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=4944913 Seven-footer Jordan makes name for self at Tulsa], ESPN, February 25, 2010.</ref>

In the 2007-08 season, Jordan finished 2nd in [[Conference USA]] in [[rebounds]] and 1st in [[field goal percentage]] and [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]]. Jordan's eight blocks against ECU tied a Conference USA Tournament record, set by Cincinnati's [[Kenyon Martin]] in the 1998 tournament. Also his 21 blocks in four Conference USA Tournament games set a new tournament record.<ref>2007-2008: [http://conferenceusa.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2007-2008/confonly.html Conference Leaders]. - Conference USA.</ref>  Jordan was rewarded with being named to the Conference USA All-Defense team.<ref>Bailey, Eric. - [http://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/extra/article.aspx?subjectID=94&tab=tu&articleid=20080312_2_B3_spanc31874 "C-USA Notebook: Jordan honored"]. - ''[[Tulsa World]]''. - March 12, 2008.</ref>  Jordan led the Golden Hurricane to the [[2008 College Basketball Invitational|2008 CBI]] championship and was named the tournament MVP.<ref>[http://proxy.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280950202 "Tulsa 70 - Bradley 64"]. - [[Associated Press]]. - (c/o [[ESPN]] - ESPN.com.) - April 4, 2008.</ref><ref>Player Bio: [http://tulsahurricane.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_jerome00.html Jerome Jordan]. - Tulsa Golden Hurricane.</ref>

In the 2008-09 season, Jordan finished 2nd in [[Conference USA]] in [[rebounds]] and 1st in [[field goal percentage]] and [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]].  He was rewarded with being named 1st team all-conference <ref>[http://www.tulsahurricane.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030909aab.html "Tulsa's Jordan and Uzoh Earn Conference USA Honors"].</ref>  On April 10, 2009, Jordan announced that he would returning for his senior season at Tulsa citing that "I think I was ready (for the NBA draft), but still have things I need to work on to become better." <ref>Bailey, Eric. - [http://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/article.aspx?subjectid=94&articleid=20090411_94_B1_Tulsas299720&archive=yes "Jordan's return is Big Boost"]. - ''[[Tulsa World]]''. - April 11, 2009.</ref>  Jordan was named the preseason 2009-10 Conference USA Player of the Year.<ref>Klein, John. [http://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/article.aspx?subjectid=203&articleid=20100312_203_B1_TUcoac6665&rss_lnk=94 Jordan helps TU find its fortitude], ''Tulsa World'', March 12, 2010.</ref>

Jordan owns the Conference USA career blocks record.<ref name="ap"/>  Jordan is considered a late first-round NBA Draft prospect.<ref name=BaileyE-TW-2009-01-31>Bailey, Eric. - "Big Man Dreams Big". - ''[[Tulsa World]]''. - January 31, 2009.</ref>
